claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

hospital_abroad.description: Whether the child is in hospital abroad.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

First, do you have any children you're asking about for Child Benefit?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have one child - my son Alex, who's 8 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions.

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. A few more questions to help assess your eligibility:

Are you the person responsible for Alex? That is, do you provide for his day-to-day needs such as food, clothes, and accommodation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm the one who looks after him day-to-day - I provide all his meals, buy his clothes, and he lives here with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Just a couple more questions to ensure I have a complete picture:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. One final question to complete my assessment:

Does Alex have any special circumstances I should know about? For example, is he currently in hospital, in care, or living away from home for any reason?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, yes - Alex is currently in hospital, but he's abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. I need to understand this situation better as it may affect your eligibility.

Could you tell me more about why Alex is abroad in hospital? Specifically, did he go abroad specifically to be in hospital, or was he abroad for another reason when he became ill?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about all those details to be honest - I just know he's in hospital abroad right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me ask a couple more questions to help clarify the situation:

1. How long has Alex been in hospital abroad?

2. Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital (for example, on things he needs, gifts, or contributing to his care)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't know exactly how long he's been there, and I'm not sure about whether I've been regularly spending money on him or not.

Based on the information you've provided, I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Here's the situation:**

Under normal circumstances, you would qualify for Child Benefit because:
- You live in the UK
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- You're responsible for his day-to-day care
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him

**However,** there's a complicating factor: Alex is currently in hospital abroad. The rules around Child Benefit when a child is in hospital abroad are complex and depend on specific circumstances:

1. **Why did Alex go abroad?** (Was it specifically for hospital treatment, or for another reason?)
2. **How long has he been in hospital?** (There's typically a 12-week limit, after which Child Benefit may stop)
3. **Are you regularly spending money on Alex?** (This can be an exception that allows Child Benefit to continue)

Without knowing these details, I cannot determine whether you would be eligible or ineligible for Child Benefit at this time.

**My recommendation:** You should contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly to discuss Alex's specific situation. They can review the details of why he's abroad, how long he's been there, and help determine whether you can continue to receive Child Benefit or if there are any exceptions that apply to your case.
